title: Don't Strike the Spark
story: In the stone bonfire-pit of Ashbarrow Hollow, the old smith keeps hammering a single stubborn spark that refuses to die. What he hasn't noticed is that Flintwhistle, the spark, SPLITS INTO FOUR every time the hammer falls. Mr 6 catches the smith's wrist mid-swing and says, "Three more swings and you'll be sweeping sparks until spring — let me count first."
question: There are 3 sparks hovering now, and each hammer strike turns every spark into 4 sparks. If the smith lands 3 more strikes, and Mr 6's frost-net then snuffs 8 sparks per second, how many seconds does the net need?
solution: Each strike multiplies the sparks by 4: 3 x 4 = 12, then 12 x 4 = 48, then 48 x 4 = 192 sparks.
The frost-net snuffs 8 sparks every second, so 192 / 8 = 24.
praise: Multiplying by 4 for each strike was precisely the right instinct — the last move was dividing that swarm by the net's speed.
hint: Do the three strikes one at a time (x4, then x4, then x4) before you let the frost-net start counting.
victory: Twenty-four seconds later the last spark went out with a tiny, insulted *pfft*. "Next time," said Mr 6, hanging up the net, "count before you clobber." The smith nodded and quietly bought himself an abacus.
imagePrompt: A cold starry night over a great stone bonfire-pit where a swarm of glowing orange sparks swirls like fireflies, a startled old smith frozen mid-swing, and a small number-six knight raising a shimmering frost-net.
